verdict.summary: Creating and connecting your own HubSpot OAuth app is quick and self-serve, and you can install it in your own account within an hour. Getting it to work for other customers is gated: installs beyond a small cap need a Marketplace listing, and certification needs real installs, a verified domain, a demo video, and a multi-month track record.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 2-4 hours to reach Gate 1 and Gate 2 (app build, test auth, AUP, domain DNS). Several days to weeks of work for Gate 3 (listing content, uninstall handling, demo video, support docs).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 minutes using the HubSpot CLI scaffold and your own super-admin account
verdict.approval_wait: None for Gates 1-2. Marketplace initial listing review: about 10 business days. Certification: response within 10 business days, full cycle should not exceed 60 days from feedback, and a six-month listing minimum (reported in the findings as an official requirement).

gates.name: Your own app and your own account (development)
gates.unlocks: Create the app with the HubSpot CLI, set your redirect URL, get client ID and secret, and connect your own HubSpot account through the OAuth flow.
limits: Legacy public apps can no longer be created in the Developer Platform UI, so use the CLI Projects path.
Installing user must be a Super Admin, or have the Marketplace access permission plus the permission groups matching the app's scopes.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes and must be refreshed with the refresh token.
Unverified apps show an install warning banner until HubSpot verifies them.

gates.name: Invited and test accounts (unlisted Marketplace app, not yet listed)
gates.unlocks: Install the app in your developer test accounts and up to 25 other accounts before listing. Private apps can be installed only in allowlisted accounts.
limits: Up to 25 installs before listing, not counting developer test accounts.
Private OAuth apps: capped at 10 allowlisted accounts (community reports 100 when created in a Solutions Partner portal).
Acceptable Use Policy must be signed before installs outside developer test accounts.
Installers of unverified apps must type 'I accept the risk' and click Connect.
One verified domain per developer account, shared by all its apps.
Static-token apps: only 1 standard account at a time, so they do not fit multi-customer use.
gates.time_to_reach: Hours to a few days, mostly for the Acceptable Use Policy and DNS domain verification

gates.name: Anyone (Marketplace listing and certification)
gates.unlocks: Public Marketplace listing with unlimited installs, and optionally certification. Sensitive Data scopes become requestable only for partners with at least one listed public app.
limits: Initial listing review: about 10 business days, with feedback if information is wrong or incomplete.
Certification: one app in review at a time; a demo video is mandatory.
Certification valid for two years on a rolling basis, then must be renewed.
Listing pricing must match the pricing on your website.
No Sensitive Data scopes in the listing.
gates.time_to_reach: Weeks to months. Listing needs at least 3 real customer production installs (community report) and a 6-month listing minimum for certification.

steps.title: Confirm your HubSpot developer account and a Super Admin test account
steps.detail: Sign in to the HubSpot Developer Platform docs and developer account. Make sure the HubSpot account you will install into is one where you are a Super Admin, or one where you hold the Marketplace access permission plus the permission groups for the scopes you request. Developer account signup and whether a developer seat is needed for a project-based app were not confirmed, so check this in the developer console.
gotchas: Developer seats are documented only for viewing or rotating static tokens, not for OAuth app creation.

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own app or can start on Composio managed auth
steps.detail: Composio lists managed OAuth for HubSpot. Start there to test flows. Move to your own HubSpot app if you need your own client ID and secret, your own redirect URI, a narrower scope set, or a Marketplace listing under your name.

steps.title: Scaffold a new project with the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Do not try to create a legacy public app in the Developer Platform UI, because that path is closed. Create a new boilerplate project with the HubSpot CLI. When prompted, choose whether the app is distributed on the Marketplace or restricted to specific accounts, and choose OAuth (not a static token).

values.label: Distribution
values.value: Marketplace (for public use) or specific accounts (for private use)

steps.title: Set the redirect URL in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In the auth block of app-hsmeta.json, set redirectUrls to the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config. Use https for production; localhost is acceptable only for local development. An agent can edit this file and check the URL format.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: If you keep localhost in the list for testing, the production redirect must still be https.

steps.title: Declare a minimal scope set in requiredScopes and optionalScopes
steps.detail: Draft the requiredScopes, conditionally required and optionalScopes arrays from the features the app really uses. Do not copy Composio's long default list. Unused scopes are flagged in Marketplace review. Move scopes used by only some users into the conditional or optional lists. The oauth scope is added automatically.
gotchas: Some CRM scopes such as custom objects require Enterprise or specific Hub tiers. Check each scope against the account tier of your test accounts.
Sensitive Data scopes are not available by default (see the sensitive-scope step).

steps.title: Upload the project and read the client credentials
steps.detail: Upload the project with the HubSpot CLI. Open the app in the developer console and go to the Auth tab. Copy the client ID and client secret and note the redirect URL shown there. You can rotate the secret on this tab. Store the secret server-side only.
gotchas: The docs show the token exchange using client_secret, so treat this as a confidential server-side client. PKCE support was not confirmed.

steps.title: Connect your own account and run a test authorization
steps.detail: Build the install URL with client_id, redirect_uri and scopes, open it in a browser, and approve as a Super Admin. HubSpot redirects back with a code parameter. Exchange the code for tokens with a form-encoded POST that includes client_id and client_secret. Check which token endpoint your flow uses before you ship (see open questions).
gotchas: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes. Test the refresh flow, not only the first token.

steps.title: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy
steps.detail: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy in the developer console. Until you sign it, you cannot install the app in accounts other than developer test accounts. This is a legal acceptance and must be done by you.

steps.title: Verify your domain with a DNS TXT record
steps.detail: Add the TXT record the developer console gives you in your domain provider's DNS settings. Verification usually completes within an hour and can take up to 48 hours. You get one verified domain per developer account, shared by all your apps, so choose the domain carefully.

steps.title: Install in test accounts and confirm the warning flow
steps.detail: Install the app in your developer test accounts and in up to 25 other accounts before listing. Expect the unverified warning and the 'I accept the risk' prompt until HubSpot verifies the app. Install counts exclude developer test accounts.

values.label: Installer must type
values.value: I accept the risk, then click Connect

gotchas: Installs beyond the pre-listing cap (25) need a Marketplace listing. Plan your customer pilot inside that cap.

steps.title: Add 429 and expired-token handling and the Uninstall App call
steps.detail: Implement retry with backoff for 429 responses and refresh the access token before it expires. Respect 100 inbound requests every 10 seconds per connected account. Call the Uninstall App endpoint when a customer removes the app. Reviewers check success rate (below 95% fails) and this uninstall flow.

steps.title: Draft listing content, support docs and the shared-data table
steps.detail: Draft the listing, pricing, support documentation and the Shared data table. Each scope the app requests must be listed with accurate read or write descriptions. Documentation must be on a public URL with no login and must cover connecting, configuring, using and uninstalling. Pricing must match your website. You review and publish the pages.

values.label: Docs requirement
values.value: Public URL, no login, covers connect, configure, use, uninstall

steps.title: Request Sensitive Data scopes only if you need them
steps.detail: Sensitive Data scopes such as crm.objects.contacts.sensitive.read must be requested from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, who may reduce the set and review your security posture. They are offered only to partners with at least one public app listed on the Marketplace, and listings must not use them. Skip them unless the product truly needs them. The current request path and timeline were not confirmed.

steps.title: Reach three real customer production installs
steps.detail: Community reports say a listing needs at least three active production installs in real customer accounts. Test and developer accounts do not count. Plan customer installs before you submit.
steps.est_time: Weeks to months, depends on your customers
gotchas: Community reports say submission is blocked under 3 active installs. Confirm this with HubSpot before you rely on it.

steps.title: Record the demo video and submit for listing and certification
steps.detail: Record a demo video that shows the connect, configure, use and uninstall flows. Submit your listing and certification request with it. Only one app can be in certification at a time. Submissions are reviewed in the order received. HubSpot responds within 10 business days and the full cycle should not exceed 60 days from feedback.
steps.est_time: 1-2 days for the video, plus review wait

requirements.item: Developer account and app created via the HubSpot CLI Projects path
requirements.detail: Legacy public app creation in the Developer Platform UI is closed, so new apps must be scaffolded with the CLI.

requirements.item: Installing user is a Super Admin, or has Marketplace access plus scope permission groups
requirements.detail: Without these permissions the installer cannot authorize the requested scopes.

requirements.item: Redirect URI registered in app-hsmeta.json auth.redirectUrls
requirements.detail: Use the Composio callback URL when using your own app with Composio. Production URLs must use https.
Required before installing in accounts other than developer test accounts.

requirements.item: Verified domain via DNS TXT record
requirements.detail: One verified domain per developer account, shared across apps. Usually within an hour, up to 48 hours.

requirements.item: Install cap before listing: 25 accounts (excluding developer test accounts)
requirements.detail: Private OAuth apps are limited to allowlisted accounts (10 per official docs context; 100 for Solutions Partner portals per a community post).
Unlimited installs apply after the app is listed. Listing review is about 10 business days.

requirements.item: OAuth plus every scope the app requests must be used
requirements.detail: Certification requires OAuth and all requested scopes in use. Extraneous scopes must be removed.

requirements.item: Demo video submitted with certification application
requirements.detail: HubSpot will not review the app without it.

requirements.item: API success rate at or above 95%
requirements.detail: Reviewers flag rates below 95%, with 429 and expired-token 401 errors as common causes.

requirements.item: Public support docs with no login and a Shared data table
requirements.detail: Docs must cover connect, configure, use and uninstall. Each requested scope documented with read/write descriptions.

requirements.item: Pricing in listing matches website pricing
Uninstall App endpoint called on removal
requirements.detail: Must be shown in the demo video.

requirements.item: Three real customer production installs before listing (community report)
requirements.detail: Test, developer and sandbox accounts do not count.

requirements.item: Six-month listing minimum and 60 active unaffiliated installs to qualify for certification
requirements.detail: Official certification page states these. Confirm whether they apply to first-time certification.

scopes.effect: Added by default to every app. You do not need to request it.
Most CRM read scopes are available on all account tiers. Check each scope in your test accounts. Read-only scopes are the easiest to justify in review.
Custom object scopes require Enterprise or specific Hub tiers. Confirm the tier before requesting.
Must be requested from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team. Only offered to partners with a listed public app. Cannot be used in Marketplace listings.
Included in Composio's default list. Remove it unless the app manages users, because unused write scopes are flagged in review. Tier not verified.

scopes.scope: Composio default scopes (e.g. accounting, e-commerce, content, sales-email-read)
scopes.effect: Composio requests a long default list. Trim it in your own app to only what is used, because extraneous scopes are flagged in Marketplace review.

blockers.symptom: Cannot create a new legacy public app in the Developer Platform UI
blockers.cause: HubSpot disabled legacy public app creation in the UI, from May 26, 2026 for newer accounts and June 23, 2026 for older ones.
blockers.fix: Create a new project with the HubSpot CLI boilerplate and choose OAuth.

blockers.symptom: Installs in other accounts fail or are refused after the first few
blockers.cause: Unlisted Marketplace OAuth apps are capped at 25 installs, and private apps at 10 allowlisted accounts. Installs outside developer test accounts also need the signed AUP.
blockers.fix: Sign the AUP and plan customer installs within the cap, or move to a Marketplace listing for unlimited installs.

blockers.symptom: Customers see an unverified-app warning and must type 'I accept the risk'
blockers.cause: The app has not yet been verified by HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team.
blockers.fix: Expect this until verification. Warn customers in your onboarding copy.

blockers.symptom: Sensitive Data scope request is refused or unavailable
blockers.cause: Sensitive Data scopes are offered only to partners with at least one listed public app, and the review may reduce them.
blockers.fix: Drop sensitive scopes from the first version. Request them later after you have a listed app.
blockers.contact: HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team (request path not verified)

blockers.symptom: Certification or listing feedback about success rate or 401 errors
blockers.cause: API success rate below 95%, with 429 burst-limit errors and expired-token 401 errors as common causes.
blockers.fix: Refresh tokens before the 30-minute expiry, retry 429s with backoff, and stay within 100 requests per 10 seconds per account.

blockers.cause: No demo video submitted, or the app does not meet certification requirements (OAuth plus all scopes used, verified domain, six-month listing, unaffiliated installs).
blockers.fix: Submit the demo video and meet every certification requirement before applying.

blockers.symptom: Listing submission is blocked with an install-count message
blockers.cause: Community reports say at least three active installs are required before submission.
blockers.fix: Get three real customer production installs. Test accounts do not count.

composio.note: Start on Composio managed auth to test flows. Move to your own HubSpot app for your own client ID and secret, your own redirect URI, a narrower scope set, or a Marketplace listing under your name. Composio's default redirect is its own callback and its default scope list is long, so trim scopes in your own app. Composio lists the token URL https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token, which differs from the 2026-09 path HubSpot documents (api.hubspot.com/oauth/2026-09/token). Verify which one your flow uses.

open_questions: Which token endpoint a Composio-brokered flow uses: Composio lists https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token, while HubSpot documents /oauth/2026-09/token on api.hubspot.com. Verify with a test authorization.
Whether HubSpot requires PKCE was not confirmed. The docs show only client_secret token exchange, so this guide assumes a confidential server-side client.
Exact refresh-token lifetime was not stated in the pages reviewed.
Whether a developer seat or developer account signup is needed to create a project-based app was not confirmed from a fetched page.
The 100-install cap for Solutions Partner portals comes only from a community post. The official install-limit page does not mention it.
The Sensitive Data request path (form link and timeline) on the current platform was not fetched. The page found dates from an older release.
The applying-for-certification form fields and the listing setup requirements page were linked but not fetched.
Real-world Marketplace approval timelines beyond the 10-business-day initial review were not found in official sources.

It is unclear whether the certification six-month listing and 60-install minimum apply to first-time certification or only to retaining status. The findings state both points but not how they interact.
The three-install listing minimum comes from community posts, not official docs. Confirm with HubSpot before planning around it.
